1240: They swept in demanding the best berth, priority docking, and a wider stretch of water than anyone else.
1241: They tipped every worker on the dock at once, then asked us all to forget the color of their coat.
1242: They demanded to dock ahead of every waiting ship and were baffled that the harbor had a waiting line at all.
1243: They handed out coins to the whole dock and asked, in return, that we behave as if we had never met them.
1244: They insisted on the grandest mooring and complained the water beneath it was not deep enough to impress.
1245: They wanted priority docking, priority unloading, and priority admiration from everyone standing nearby.
1246: They tipped the dock crew so lavishly that three of them applauded before remembering they had never seen them.
1247: They swept past the harbor line, took the finest berth, and asked me to move the other ships further out of sight.
1248: They paid to dock first and paid again for the harbor to pretend the docking had never taken place.
1249: They demanded the whole pier be cleared for their arrival, as if the other boats were merely decoration.
1250: They arrived tossing coins to everyone on the dock and asking, with each coin, that we forget the face that gave it.
1251: They wanted priority docking so badly they offered to buy the harbor, the pier, and the tide itself.
1252: They tipped the entire dock, then grew annoyed that our gratitude was not grand enough for the amount.
1253: They demanded the best berth, cut ahead of a dozen boats, and asked why anyone else was even allowed to dock.
1254: They swept in, tipped everyone, and requested that the harbor bell ring only for their arrival from now on.
1255: They paid the whole crew to say nothing, then paid a little more to say something flattering instead.
1256: They took the priority mooring meant for arriving ships and asked if I had a priority above priority.
1257: They tipped the dock so generously that even the seabirds seemed to expect something, and got nothing.
1258: They demanded to dock at once and treated the waiting ships as an unforgivable insult to their schedule.
1259: They claimed the grandest berth, then asked whether the harbor could be persuaded to look a little more impressed.
1260: They swept up to my desk, announced they had nothing to declare, and every bag clinked like a box of coins.
1261: I asked if they had anything valuable. They laughed, said no, and three of their suitcases jingled at once.
1262: Nothing to declare, they insisted, while a bag of theirs quietly rang like a purse full of gold.
1263: I waved them to the green lane. Even their coat pockets clinked when they strolled past me.
1264: They set a heavy case on my table, swore it held only clothes, and it chimed when I nudged it.
1265: The most honest traveller alive, they said. Then they bowed, and a fortune rattled somewhere on them.
1266: They declared exactly nothing, tipped me not to open a single bag, and every bag clinked as they left.
1267: I asked their bags to please stop clinking. The traveller assured me the bags were empty. They were not.
1268: They breezed through in the finest coat I've seen, declaring nothing, jingling everything.
1269: Nothing to declare, they said, patting a suitcase that answered back with a small metallic song.
1270: They handed me their form: all blank. Their luggage, meanwhile, rang like a jar stuffed full of loose coins.
1271: I've stamped a thousand travellers. None ever clinked this richly while claiming to own nothing.
1272: They complained the line was beneath them, declared no valuables, and clinked past me like a treasure chest.
1273: The stranger swore the bags held only socks. Socks, it turns out, do not clink when you set them down.
1274: They wore rings on every finger, told me they had nothing of worth, and jingled with each grand gesture.
1275: Nothing to declare, they repeated, slower, as if I were the strange one for hearing all that clinking.
1276: They demanded to skip the whole inspection, then swept off, their bags singing with hidden metal.
1277: I offered to help lift a case. It weighed like an anchor and clinked, and they said it was just papers.
1278: They breezed up, all velvet and confidence, declaring nothing while a small fortune rattled at their side.
1279: The traveller signed the form 'honest', tipped me lavishly to hurry, and clinked out the door.
